q: The Yorke-Li theorem ('Period Three Implies Chaos', 1975) states that for a continuous map f: [a,b] → [a,b]:
opts: Existence of a fixed point implies chaos
If f has a period-3 orbit, then f has periodic orbits of all periods and uncountably many irregular (non-periodic) points
Period-3 implies the map is topologically conjugate to the tent map
exp: Li-Yorke theorem: period-3 → all periods. More precisely, the theorem produces a 'scrambled set' of uncountably many points with irregular orbits (pairs asymptotically independent but not asymptotically separate). This is the Li-Yorke definition of chaos.
